_comment: Task 52b golden replay baselines. Both missions are the exact same seed-1, 8-operator (4v4) fixture built through Sandata.Headless.HeadlessRunner.BuildOpenGrid(8) and Sandata.Headless.HeadlessRunner.BuildInitialState(8, 1, packingSide) -- the same dense, alternating-faction packing HeadlessRunnerTests and the seed-1 benchmark workload use -- ticked for 40 ticks with MissionTickPolicy.StateHashCadenceTicks=1 and TickLimit=1000. EmptyOrderStream submits no orders (the pure autonomous case). NonEmptyOrderStream submits, at tick 0 through SandataSimulation.SubmitOrder: a MoveAlongPath order for faction 0's entity 1 along the two-node path (4,4)->(12,4), and a Hold order for faction 1's entity 2. Both orders were accepted (no rejection). Every hash below was measured by running a temporary capture test (removed once these values were recorded), never calculated or typed by hand. TickStateHashesHex[i] is SandataSimulation.LastStateHash immediately after RunTick(i), formatted X16.
_rerecorded2026-08-11a: First re-measurement of the day, when SandataSimulation.RunTick began writing MissionState.Tick. Until then nothing in Sandata.Core ever wrote that field, so it stayed 0 for a whole run: SandataStateHasher folded a constant and every emitted event carried tick 0 regardless of when it fired. Both tick-0 state hashes were byte-identical across that change, which was its expected signature -- on tick 0 the field was already 0, so only tick 1 onward could move.
_rerecorded2026-08-11b: Second re-measurement, and the values below are from it. Two changes landed together. (1) HeadlessRunner.BuildInitialState now assigns a firearm: every fourth operator carries FirearmId.Beretta92Fs and the rest carry FirearmId.Ak47. Before this nothing in src/ assigned OperatorState.Firearm at all, so every operator in every run carried the default Ak47 and the roster in play was one weapon. (2) SandataSimulation stage 9 now halts an operator that stage 8 gave OperatorIntent.Engage when its best contact is inside its firearm's MaxEffectiveWu, so an operator in a position to shoot stands still to do it instead of walking into the body it is shooting at. Unlike the first re-measurement, the tick-0 hashes move too: the loadout is part of the initial state and SandataStateHasher folds OperatorState.Firearm. NEITHER change is a new SandataPresetId. Design section 4's trigger list is an enum value or order, a roster order, a weapon weight, the tick rate, the millisecond conversion rule, or a hash mixer. The FirearmId enum, the FirearmCatalog rows, and FirearmRuleset.ContentHash (12611003062847309889) are all untouched -- this only chooses which existing rows the workload uses -- and SandataRuleset.ContentHash is unchanged at 8955292433887190872.
